name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.179.0 — A bound mock's screen now names the record it shows: an element carrying `data-record="<entity>[i].<field>"` must resolve to a real record field, and its visible text must equal the resolved value exactly, catching the ninth retyped copy of a customer's name that the old any-seed-value check could never see. A distinctive seed value shown outside every bound element — one with a space or at least eight characters, occurring in exactly one record across all record files — is refused; every other stray value warns. The rules bind on the same labelled, wire-register-linked mock predicate the invention checks use, warning at journey-drawn and refusing at journey-approved, alongside the unchanged journey-level placeholder check. ADR-0023 records the ruling and narrows ADR-0013's records paragraph to match. 7.178.0 — The region-note layer now owns one interaction mode at a time — idle, arming, drawing or composing, written only through setMode — with pointer capture on the overlay itself replacing three document-level listeners and a click-swallowing shield, named exits from every drag (Escape, a sub-12px release, pointercancel, lostpointercapture), and drag geometry clamped to the mock document before capture. Affordances (cursor, pointer-events, touch-action, the marking scrim) derive from the overlay's own data-mode in viewer.css instead of imperative style writes, box selection reconciles by id instead of rebuilding the layer, and reveal (scroll + pulse) fires only when a selection did not originate on the clicked box itself, with viewer.css now shipping the pulse keyframes and the has-sel dim rule the approved prototype always specified. On the review page, a framed board's note and draft cards are built by the frame but placed by the host page in its own document at full, unscaled size beside — never over — the box, so a card no longer renders unreadably small under a board's CSS scale. 7.177.0 — The replay tree is the reviewed tree: each review now records the two commits bounding what it judged as refs under refs/spec-review/<runId>/ — judged at the close row's head sha, close at the close commit — written best-effort so a failed write can never block a close. The replay harness reads that pair instead of asking which commit last touched the spec file, refuses (exit 4) a row that cannot name its own bounds, and reconstructs the pre-ref backlog only through the new run-once replay.js --backfill-pins. Setup re-derives the target's own AC coverage against the tree it assembled and exits 5 with a diagnosis rather than printing a success line over a tree the review never saw.
